biography.plain_text: Steven Sablotsky is an American chemical engineer who founded Noven Pharmaceuticals, a developer of drug-delivery patches. A University of Florida graduate, he helped develop the Nitro-Dur II nitroglycerin patch at Key Pharmaceuticals before starting Noven with his cousin Mitchell Goldberg. He later founded Ocean Research Corporation to investigate potentially useful marine compounds.

long_biography.plain_text:
Pharmaceutical entrepreneur Steven Sablotsky first studied how to extract more oil from underground deposits. His graduate research examined surfactants, boundary layers and the forces governing movement between materials. He later applied those chemical-engineering principles to delivering medicines through the skin, drawing on business training as well as laboratory knowledge.

He also helped neurobiologist Leonid Moroz test a mobile laboratory at sea. Sablotsky supplied a research-equipped vessel and crew without charge and joined an expedition himself. The project let researchers analyse fragile marine organisms shortly after collecting them, sending sequencing data by satellite to the University of Florida's supercomputer.
